correctness.rationale: For the exact two-buffer cyclic update, the computed three-dimensional two-step matrix has the stated cubic. Its strict Schur–Jury inequalities factor into two positive terms, a positive multiple of F(t), and the determinant constraint. The smaller positive F-root precedes the determinant boundary, giving the exact cutoff; endpoints follow by substitution. E+TE spans the augmented state, so initialized trajectories cannot all converge when the matrix is non-Schur. Five SymPy identities, 500 exact-rational direct-cycle tests, 3000 finite eigenvalue comparisons, and limiting cases passed; infinite assertions rely on analytic proof.

value.rationale: A nonseparable strongly convex quadratic is the simplest natural test of the design tradeoff between stale-gradient reuse and coordinate coupling. The complete exact admissible-step classification identifies an initially counterintuitive and practically actionable reversal: no-memory cyclic descent permits t<2, while partial fading memory permits t>2 exactly when gamma<1/2 and c^2>1/[2(1-gamma)]. A globally sharp supremum t=3 (unattained for SPD systems) quantifies the effect. This is a motivated method-specific stability phase diagram, not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere algebraic rearrangement.
